title: GraphCAD: Geometry-Aware Diffusion on Edge-Adjacency Graphs for CAD Generation
title_zh: GraphCAD：基于边邻接图的几何感知扩散CAD生成

paragraphs.en: Generative modeling for Computer-Aided Design (CAD) remains fundamentally challenged by the need to capture the intricate interplay between discrete topological connectivity and precise spatial geometry inherent in Boundary Representations (B-reps). Existing generative approaches largely formulate CAD construction as a sequence modeling problem, but consequently lack an explicit topological inductive bias. In this work, we present GraphCAD , a geometry-aware generative framework that centers modeling on the Edge-Adjacency Graph (EAG), a novel graph-based CAD representation tailored for generative tasks. GraphCAD adopts a hybrid graph diffusion formulation to jointly model the discrete and continuous components of EAG and introduces a geometry-aware denoising mechanism that “ renders ” node attributes into spatial point sets. These point sets are encoded by an SE(3)-equivariant backbone and fused into the node representations, thereby grounding the generative process in physical geometry. To support this study, we construct EAGBench, a large-scale dataset of engineering CAD models. Extensive experiments show that GraphCAD can generate complex CAD models with more than 50 faces and achieves state-of-the-art performance in geometric fidelity and distributional alignment compared with sequence-based baselines.
paragraphs.zh: 计算机辅助设计（CAD）的生成式建模仍然面临根本性挑战，即如何捕捉边界表示（B-reps）中固有的离散拓扑连接与精确空间几何之间错综复杂的相互作用。 现有的生成式方法大多将 CAD 构建表述为序列建模问题，因而缺乏显式的拓扑归纳偏置。 在本工作中，我们提出了 GraphCAD，这是一个几何感知的生成式框架，其建模核心是边邻接图（EAG），一种专为生成式任务定制的新型基于图的 CAD 表示。 GraphCAD 采用混合图扩散公式来联合建模 EAG 的离散与连续组件，并引入一种几何感知的去噪机制，将节点属性“渲染”为空间点集。 这些点集由一个 SE(3) 等变的主干网络进行编码，并融合到节点表示中，从而使生成过程立足于真实的物理几何。 为支持本研究，我们构建了 EAGBench，一个大规模工程 CAD 模型数据集。 大量实验表明，GraphCAD 能够生成超过 50 个面的复杂 CAD 模型，并且与基于序列的基线方法相比，在几何保真度和分布对齐方面达到了最先进的性能。

paragraphs.en: The foundation of modern engineering and manufacturing depends critically on Computer-Aided Design (CAD) models for the rigorous specification of physical objects ( Shivegowda et al., 2022 ; Deng et al., 2025 ; Su et al., 2026 ) . Although automating the synthesis of such models is highly desirable for accelerating design workflows, the inherently hybrid structure of CAD data makes this problem particularly challenging ( Patel et al., 2006 ; Chen et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025c ) . In practice, CAD data is most commonly represented in the Boundary Representation (B-rep) format ( Jayaraman et al., 2023 ) , which defines 3D models through parameterized faces, edges, and vertices, jointly encoding the geometric and topological information necessary for a complete description of the shape ( Jones et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2025 ; Lee et al., 2025 ) . As a result, directly synthesizing B-reps remains notoriously difficult, since it requires modeling continuous geometric parameters and discrete topological connectivity in a unified manner ( Guo et al., 2022 ; Liu et al., 2024b ; Liu et al., 2024a ) .
paragraphs.zh: 现代工程与制造的基础在很大程度上依赖于计算机辅助设计（CAD）模型来对物理对象进行严格的规格描述（Shivegowda et al., 2022; Deng et al., 2025; Su et al., 2026）。 尽管自动化合成此类模型对于加速设计工作流程极具价值，但CAD数据固有的混合结构使这一问题尤为困难（Patel et al., 2006; Chen et al., 2025; Li et al., 2025c）。 在实践中，CAD数据最常以边界表示（B-rep）格式表示（Jayaraman et al., 2023），该格式通过参数化的面、边和顶点来定义三维模型，共同编码完整描述形状所需的几何与拓扑信息（Jones et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2025; Lee et al., 2025）。 因此，直接合成B-rep仍然出了名地困难，因为它需要以统一的方式对连续的几何参数和离散的拓扑连接进行建模（Guo et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2024b; Liu et al., 2024a）。

paragraphs.en: Prevailing approaches typically model B-reps either as sequences of commands ( Li et al., 2022 ; Ren et al., 2022 ; Khan et al., 2024a ) or as Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) programs ( Ren et al., 2021 ; Sharma et al., 2018 ; Yu et al., 2023 ) . While these paradigms are intuitive, they often struggle to preserve strict topological integrity ( Xu et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2025b ) . In sequence-based generation, for example, a small error in an early operation can propagate through the entire construction process, ultimately producing disjoint loops, non-manifold edges, or entirely invalid geometries. More recently, methods such as BrepGiff ( Guo et al., 2025 ) and GraphBRep ( Lai et al., 2025 ) have sought to mitigate these topological issues by abstracting B-reps into Face-Adjacency Graphs ( Jayaraman et al., 2021 ) . By leveraging the structural advantages of graph representations, these methods have shown promising results. However, because they typically rely on UV-domain sampling to approximate geometry and do not explicitly anchor generation to a 1D wireframe scaffold, they remain limited in enforcing the precise boundary constraints required for high-fidelity industrial CAD models.
paragraphs.zh: 主流方法通常将 B-rep 建模为命令序列（Li et al., 2022；Ren et al., 2022；Khan et al., 2024a）或构造实体几何（CSG）程序（Ren et al., 2021；Sharma et al., 2018；Yu et al., 2023）。 尽管这些范式直观易懂，但它们往往难以保持严格的拓扑完整性（Xu et al., 2024；Li et al., 2025b）。 例如，在基于序列的生成中，早期操作中的一个小误差可能会在整个构建过程中传播，最终产生不连续的环、非流形边或完全无效的几何体。 最近，BrepGiff（Guo et al., 2025）和 GraphBRep（Lai et al., 2025）等方法试图通过将 B-rep 抽象为面邻接图（Jayaraman et al., 2021）来缓解这些拓扑问题。 通过利用图表示的结构优势，这些方法已经展现出可喜的成果。 然而，由于它们通常依赖 UV 域采样来近似几何，并且没有将生成过程明确锚定到一维线框骨架上，因此在执行高保真工业 CAD 模型所需的精确边界约束方面仍然存在局限。

paragraphs.en: To address these limitations, we revisit prevailing graph formulations and introduce GraphCAD. In contrast to prior approaches based on Face-Adjacency Graphs, where nodes correspond to complex trimmed surfaces, our method adopts a new graph construction paradigm centered on 1D wireframe edges. Specifically, we propose the Edge-Adjacency Graph (EAG) , which redefines the fundamental graph unit from faces to edges. Under this formulation, each node represents a topological edge augmented with hybrid attributes, including curve types and spatial parameters.
paragraphs.zh: 为了解决这些局限性，我们重新审视了主流的图表示方法，并提出了 GraphCAD。 与先前基于面邻接图的方法不同——这些方法中的节点对应于复杂的裁剪曲面——我们的方法采用了一种以一维线框边为核心的新图构建范式。 具体而言，我们提出了边邻接图（EAG），它将图的基本单元从面重新定义为边。 在这种表示下，每个节点表示一条拓扑边，并带有混合属性，包括曲线类型和空间参数。

paragraphs.en: To synthesize the proposed EAG representation, GraphCAD employs a geometry-aware hybrid graph diffusion framework. To accommodate the heterogeneous nature of EAG, we formulate a hybrid diffusion process that jointly models the distribution of discrete topological attributes and continuous geometric parameters. Unlike standard graph diffusion models, which treat node attributes as independent numerical vectors, our method explicitly interprets them as spatial geometry. During diffusion, we “ render ” the numerical attributes associated with topological B-rep edges into 3D curves, sample local point sets from these curves, and encode them with an SE(3)-equivariant backbone. This design grounds abstract parameters in their physical realization, enabling the model to capture the intricate interplay between topological connectivity and geometric fidelity inherent to the EAG representation. To validate our approach, we introduce EAGBench, a large-scale unified dataset constructed by aggregating and standardizing component-level B-reps from existing repositories such as DeepCAD ( Wu et al., 2021 ) and the Fusion 360 Gallery ( Willis et al., 2021 ) .

paragraphs.en: The generation of CAD models has attracted increasing attention in recent years ( Xu et al., 2023 ; Rukhovich et al., 2025 ; Casey et al., 2025 ) . Early approaches often represented CAD shapes using Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) ( Yin et al., 2020 ; Yu et al., 2022 ; Mews et al., 2025 ) . Although theoretically expressive, CSG-based methods are generally regarded as overly complex and insufficiently flexible for typical industrial design scenarios ( Andújar et al., 2022 ) . As a result, much of the recent literature has shifted toward feature-based modeling paradigms in which shapes are represented as sequences of commands ( Wang et al., 2025 ; Yuan et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025a ; Xu et al., 2022 ) . Recent methods such as Text2CAD ( Khan et al., 2024b ) and CADDreamer ( Li et al., 2025d ) have substantially improved controllability and geometric fidelity within this paradigm. Nevertheless, these approaches still rely on sequential or implicit formulations. Because they primarily encode command histories rather than explicit geometric-topological structure, they offer limited direct access to topological and geometric information and therefore lack an explicit topological inductive bias. Consequently, a critical gap remains for generative methods that can directly synthesize robust CAD representations.

paragraphs.en: Boundary Representation (B-rep) defines a solid through geometric primitives, such as parametric curves and surfaces, together with topological entities including vertices, edges, and faces ( Lou et al., 2023 ) . While discrete representations, such as point clouds ( Qi et al., 2017 ) , voxels ( Wu et al., 2015 ) , meshes ( Hanocka et al., 2019 ) , and sequences ( Ganin et al., 2021 ) , have been extensively studied, they lack the exact geometric precision required for engineering design. To bridge the gap between deep learning and precise CAD modeling, prior work has sought to encode B-reps into learnable graph structures ( Colligan et al., 2022 ; Xia et al., 2024 ; Dai et al., 2025 ) . UV-Net ( Jayaraman et al., 2021 ) pioneered the representation of B-reps as Face-Adjacency Graphs (FAGs), in which nodes are associated with 2D surface features extracted from UV grids. This face-centric formulation was later adopted and extended by generative methods such as BrepGiff ( Guo et al., 2025 ) and GraphBRep ( Lai et al., 2025 ) , which leverage graph structures to preserve complex topological relationships during generation. However, because these methods typically represent nodes as complex trimmed surfaces and decompose generation into multiple submodules, they often suffer from computational redundancy, error accumulation across stages, and substantial difficulty in enforcing precise 1D boundary constraints.

paragraphs.en: Diffusion models ( Ho et al., 2020 ; Dhariwal and Nichol, 2021 ) have achieved state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of generative tasks. In the graph domain, methods such as GDSS ( Jo et al., 2022 ) and DiGress ( Vignac et al., 2023 ) have successfully extended diffusion modeling to continuous and discrete graph structures, respectively. However, applying these generic frameworks to CAD requires addressing domain-specific engineering constraints, particularly the physical symmetries of 3D space. SE(3)-equivariant networks ( Fuchs et al., 2020 ) have demonstrated strong effectiveness in applications such as molecular dynamics by ensuring robustness to rotations. In this work, we bring these advances into the CAD domain. Building upon discrete graph diffusion, we develop an SE(3)-equivariant hybrid model specifically tailored to the Edge-Adjacency Graph. This design enables the generation of rigorous engineering geometries with invariant likelihoods, a property that remains largely overlooked in existing graph generative models.

paragraphs.en: We present a novel generative framework for CAD models (see Figure 2 ). To introduce a stronger topological inductive bias in sequence-based methods, we shift the representation paradigm from parametric CAD sequences to the Edge-Adjacency Graph (EAG). This formulation introduces strong structural inductive biases that naturally promote topological integrity and, in turn, improve generation quality. Based on this representation, we develop a geometry-aware hybrid graph diffusion model that jointly generates both structural connectivity and precise 3D geometry, treating them as physical spatial entities rather than independent abstract variables.

paragraphs.en: We evaluate our framework against two categories of baselines to assess both topological correctness and geometric fidelity. For graph generation , we compare against state-of-the-art autoregressive and diffusion-based models, including GraphNVP ( Madhawa et al., 2019 ) , GDSS ( Jo et al., 2022 ) , ConGress ( Vignac et al., 2023 ) , and DiGress ( Vignac et al., 2023 ) , to validate the structural quality of the generated EAGs. For CAD generation , we benchmark against DeepCAD ( Wu et al., 2021 ) , a representative sequence-based method, as well as Text2CAD ( Khan et al., 2024b ) and TGBFN ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) . We further compare with graph-based CAD generation methods, including BrepGiff ( Guo et al., 2025 ) and GraphBRep ( Lai et al., 2025 ) .

paragraphs.en: We employ a comprehensive set of metrics covering both graph topology and geometric fidelity. To further assess distributional alignment and generative diversity, we report the Jensen-Shannon Divergence ( JSD ) and the Minimum Matching Distance ( MMD ). paragraphs.en: We implement a hybrid graph diffusion framework with T = 500 T=500 timesteps. The SE(3)-equivariant VNEncoder processes local point sets via a three-stage hierarchy (32, 64, 128 channels) using VN-LeakyReLU activations. paragraphs.en: We categorize reconstruction failures into four primary types, as illustrated in Fig. 4 : (i) degenerate primitives (Fig. 4 a), where coincident endpoints ( 𝐩 start ≈ 𝐩 end \mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{start}}\approx\mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{end}} ) produce zero-length edges that cannot be incorporated into the B-rep wireframe; (ii) undefined arc parametrization (Fig. 4 b), where collinear 𝐩 start \mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{start}} , 𝐩 end \mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{end}} , and 𝐩 center \mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{center}} fail to uniquely determine the plane and curvature of an arc or circle; (iii) geometric inconsistency (Fig. 4 c), where the constraint ∥ 𝐩 start − 𝐩 center ∥ ≈ ∥ 𝐩 end − 𝐩 center ∥ \lVert\mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{start}}-\mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{center}}\rVert\approx\lVert\mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{end}}-\mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{center}}\rVert is violated beyond the CAD kernel tolerance, resulting in invalid primitives; and (iv) topological mismatch (Fig. 4 d), where graph-connected edges have non-coincident endpoints, producing an open wire that fails the watertightness check required for solid B-rep construction.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将重建失败归为四种主要类型，如图 4 所示：(i) 退化图元（图 4 a），其中重合的端点（ 𝐩 start ≈ 𝐩 end \mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{start}}\approx\mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{end}} ）产生无法纳入 B-rep 线框的零长度边；(ii) 未定义的圆弧参数化（图 4 b），其中共线的 𝐩 start \mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{start}} 、 𝐩 end \mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{end}} 和 𝐩 center \mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{center}} 无法唯一确定圆弧或圆的平面和曲率；(iii) 几何不一致（图 4 c），其中约束 ∥ 𝐩 start − 𝐩 center ∥ ≈ ∥ 𝐩 end − 𝐩 center ∥ \lVert\mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{start}}-\mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{center}}\rVert\approx\lVert\mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{end}}-\mathbf{p}_{\mathrm{center}}\rVert 超出 CAD 内核容差而被违反，导致图元无效；以及 (iv) 拓扑不匹配（图 4 d），其中图中相连的边端点不重合，形成开放的线框，无法通过实体 B-rep 构建所要求的水密性检查。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate the ability of GraphCAD to capture the latent distribution of Edge-Adjacency Graphs (EAGs). As shown in Table 1 , GraphCAD consistently outperforms both flow-based (GraphNVP) and diffusion-based (GDSS, ConGress, DiGress) baselines across all evaluation metrics. In particular, our model achieves the lowest Deg, Clus, and Orb scores, indicating a closer match to the reference topological distribution. The advantage is especially pronounced on the more challenging EAGBench-FS benchmark: whereas the strongest baseline, DiGress, attains a validity of 77.45 % 77.45\% , GraphCAD preserves a substantially higher validity of 96.58 % 96.58\% . This large margin suggests that our geometry-aware formulation is particularly effective at modeling the intricate connectivity constraints inherent in engineering components.

paragraphs.en: On the more challenging EAGBench-FS benchmark, GraphCAD consistently outperforms all baselines across all five metrics. Our method achieves the lowest IR ( 5.42 % 5.42\% ), CD ( 3.37 3.37 ), HD ( 0.59 0.59 ), JSD ( 64.97 64.97 ), and MMD ( 3.52 3.52 ), surpassing both sequence-based methods, such as Text2CAD, and graph-based methods such as GraphBRep and BrepGiff. paragraphs.en: To validate our architectural design, we compare GraphCAD against variants lacking specific components. The results in Table 3 confirm the necessity of each module. paragraphs.en: Several limitations remain. First, EAG models 1D boundary curves rather than explicit 2D surface patches. Although it supports curved boundaries and non-planar surfaces through line, arc, and circle primitives, complete surface definitions, such as NURBS control points, are recovered through post-processing. This reconstruction may introduce errors in regions with complex curvature. Second, the iterative diffusion process requires T T denoising steps, making inference slower than single-pass generative methods. Finally, our experiments focus on component-level parts. Scaling EAG generation to large assemblies with thousands of topological edges remains challenging because of the substantially larger discrete state space.

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we introduced GraphCAD, a geometry-aware hybrid graph diffusion framework for CAD generation built upon the proposed Edge-Adjacency Graph (EAG) representation. By combining a curve rendering mechanism with an SE(3)-equivariant backbone, our model grounds abstract node attributes in spatial geometry, thereby promoting robust topological and geometric consistency. Extensive experiments on the EAGBench benchmark demonstrate that GraphCAD achieves state-of-the-art performance in both validity and fidelity compared with existing sequence-based and graph-based baselines. In future work, we plan to extend this probabilistic formulation to infer full surface definitions, moving beyond wireframe generation toward complete solid reconstruction.
paragraphs.zh: 在本文中，我们提出了 GraphCAD，一种基于所提出的边-邻接图（EAG）表示的几何感知混合图扩散 CAD 生成框架。 通过将曲线渲染机制与 SE(3) 等变骨干网络相结合，我们的模型将抽象节点属性锚定于空间几何，从而促进稳健的拓扑与几何一致性。 在 EAGBench 基准上的大量实验表明，与现有的基于序列和基于图的基线相比，GraphCAD 在有效性和保真度方面均达到了最先进的性能。 在未来的工作中，我们计划将这一概率公式扩展到推断完整的曲面定义，从线框生成迈向完整的实体重建。
